title: Estimate Your Salary After Tax Australia: Hourly to Annual with Casual Loading and Super
description: Convert your hourly rate to annual pay, including casual loading and super. Use our guide to estimate salary after tax Australia for 2026–27.
salarySummary: For a full-time worker on the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour, working 38 hours per week, the annual gross pay is about $52,269 before tax and super.

faqs.q: How do I convert my hourly rate to an annual salary?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work each week, then by 52 weeks. For a standard full-time role of 38 hours per week, the formula is: hourly rate × 38 × 52. This gives your gross annual pay before tax and super. If you work fewer or more hours, adjust the weekly hours accordingly.

faqs.q: What is casual loading and how does it affect my pay?
faqs.a: Casual loading is an extra 25% paid on top of the base hourly rate to compensate for not receiving paid leave entitlements. For example, the National Minimum Wage for casuals is $33.05 per hour (base $26.44 plus 25%). When using our timesheet, tick the casual loading checkbox and enter your base rate – the calculator adds the 25% automatically.

faqs.q: How is superannuation calculated and is it included in my salary?
faqs.a: Superannuation is paid on top of your ordinary earnings at a rate of 12% (from 1 July 2026). It is not deducted from your salary; your employer adds it separately. The super guarantee applies up to a maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. Our estimate shows super as an additional amount, not part of your take-home pay.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding Your Hourly to Annual Conversion

When you receive an hourly rate or a salary offer, knowing what that means as an annual figure helps you compare jobs and plan your finances. The standard formula is straightforward: multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work each week, then by 52 weeks in a year. For most full-time roles, we assume a 38-hour week, as set by the Fair Work Commission for the National Minimum Wage. This gives you your gross annual salary before tax, super, and any deductions.

For example, if your base hourly rate is $30.00 and you work 38 hours per week, your annual gross pay is $30.00 × 38 × 52 = $59,280. If you are a casual employee, you also receive a 25% casual loading on top of your base rate, making your effective hourly rate $37.50. In that case, the annual calculation uses the loaded rate: $37.50 × 38 × 52 = $74,100. Always start with your base rate – our [timesheet](/topics/casual-loading) has a checkbox to add casual loading automatically.

## Breaking Down Your Pay: Fortnightly and Weekly

It can be helpful to see your pay in smaller chunks. Your weekly pay is simply your hourly rate multiplied by your weekly hours. For a 38-hour week at $30.00 per hour, that’s $1,140 per week. Your fortnightly pay is double that: $2,280. Many employers pay fortnightly, so knowing this figure helps you budget. The annual figure is then weekly × 52 or fortnightly × 26. Our [reference tables](/data) provide quick conversions for common rates.

## The National Minimum Wage and Award Rates

The Fair Work Commission sets the National Minimum Wage each year. From 1 July 2026, the minimum is $26.44 per hour for a full-time adult employee, or $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours. Casual employees receive a 25% loading, making their minimum $33.05 per hour. However, many industries have award rates that are higher than the minimum. Awards are legal documents that set minimum pay and conditions for specific jobs. If you work under an award, your base rate must be at least the award rate. Our [pay guides](/blog) explain how to find your correct award classification.

## Casual Loading Explained

Casual loading is an extra payment to compensate for not receiving paid sick leave, annual leave, or public holidays. It is 25% of the base hourly rate. When using our calculator, never enter a rate that already includes casual loading – enter your base rate and tick the casual loading checkbox. The system adds the 25% on top. For example, if your base award rate is $28.00, your casual rate becomes $35.00. This loaded rate is then used to calculate your weekly, fortnightly, and annual pay.

## Superannuation: Paid on Top

Superannuation is a compulsory contribution your employer makes to your retirement fund. From 1 July 2026, the super guarantee rate is 12% of your ordinary earnings. Importantly, super is paid on top of your salary, not deducted from it. So if your gross annual salary is $59,280, your employer also contributes an additional $7,113.60 in super (12% of $59,280), up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. Our estimate includes super as a separate figure. For more details, see our page on [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging).

## Estimating Your Salary After Tax Australia

To understand your take-home pay, you need to deduct tax and the Medicare levy. The Australian Taxation Office uses a progressive tax scale for residents in 2026–27:
- Nil tax on income up to $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

Plus, the Medicare levy is generally 2% of your taxable income. Using the example of $59,280 gross annual salary, your estimated tax would be approximately $9,667 and Medicare $1,186, leaving you with about $48,427 after tax. This is your estimated salary after tax Australia. Note that this estimate uses the 2025–26 Medicare reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed here. It does not include HELP repayments, the Medicare levy surcharge, or salary packaging.

## Average Earnings and Comparisons

The Australian Bureau of Statistics publishes Average Weekly Earnings. For May 2026, full-time adult ordinary time earnings were $2,083.70 per week, or about $108,352 per year. All employees (including part-time) earned $1,579.20 per week on average. These are averages across all industries and states, not the median for any specific job. If you want to compare your pay to industry averages, see our [average pay](/topics/average-pay) page.

## Important Disclaimer

Our annual pay estimate is hourly rate × hours per week × 52. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax uses the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax. For a personalised calculation, use our [timesheet](/) to enter your exact hours and rate.

## Using Our Tools

Our [timesheet](/) is the home page where you type your base hourly rate. A checkbox adds 25% casual loading on top – never enter a rate that already includes loading. The tool then shows your weekly, fortnightly, and annual gross pay, plus estimated tax, Medicare, and super. For more detailed pay guides and award information, visit our [pay guides](/blog) section. You can also explore [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage) and [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) topics for further reading.
